ui.Compares your actual routed spend with t: Compares your actual routed spend with the estimated cost of using only the most expensive model configured in the auto-router. It accounts for both the cache savings from staying on one model and the added cache costs from switching models.
ui.Controls randomness. Lower values make o: Controls randomness. Lower values make output more deterministic, higher values more creative.

ui.Headroom is a native LiteLLM guardrail t: Headroom is a native LiteLLM guardrail that compresses your prompts before they reach the model, so you pay for fewer input tokens. The tokens it removes are priced and shown on the Usage tab as compression savings.

ui.Shuffle between deployments within this: Shuffle between deployments within this % of the lowest latency. Default - 0 (i.e. always pick lowest latency).
ui.Spend on requests that invoked each tool: Spend on requests that invoked each tool (MCP and client-side tools); declaring a tool without invoking it does not count. A request that invoked multiple tools counts its full spend toward each, so this attributes rather than partitions spend.

ui.This agent cannot be updated or deleted: This agent cannot be updated or deleted here (missing model id). Manage it from Models & Endpoints.
ui.Track and configure the mechanisms that: Track and configure the mechanisms that save you money: prompt compression and prompt caching. Auto routers live under Models + Endpoints, on the Auto-Routers tab
ui.Turns each tier served. Turns the classi: Turns each tier served. Turns the classifier sent to the default model belong to no tier and are not counted here, so this can total less than the router's turns.
ui.What caching saved against paying the in: What caching saved against paying the input rate for every token: the discount on tokens served from cache, less the premium providers charge to write a cache entry. Can be negative on traffic that writes more cache than it reuses.
ui.What this traffic would have cost had ev: What this traffic would have cost had every request gone to the most expensive model the auto-router can route to, minus what it actually cost. Switching leaves the new model with a cold cache, so it pays to write the prompt again while the baseline is priced as already warm; a route that thrashes the cache can total below zero, and a genuine first turn, where neither side had anything cached, is undercounted.
ui.Would the auto-router have answered as w: Would the auto-router have answered as well as the models you use today? Find out on your real traffic, before switching anything.
ui.are named collections of specific tools: are named collections of specific tools from one or more MCP servers. Instead of exposing all tools from a server, a toolset gives an agent exactly the tools it needs.
ui.sending large volumes of uncached input: sending large volumes of uncached input with a low cache hit rate are likely missing prompt caching. Potential savings is approximate: uncached input priced at what your cached traffic nets per cached token, after cache-write premiums.
ui.share of all measured turns that missed: share of all measured turns that missed cache because a return to an earlier tier came after its TTL lapsed
ui.to start a realtime session. You can spe: to start a realtime session. You can speak using your microphone or type messages. The AI will respond with voice and text.
